coverage_limitations: Assembly is matched lexically (labels and .global directives): the scanner cannot prove what an assembly routine does with a register-held ID.

Struct-typed data instances (for example the ~730 struct UnitDefinition blobs in src/events_udefs.c) are audited through their struct type hits, not once per instance; only scalar-element arrays and ID-record tables are enumerated as data symbols.
Function bodies are not analysed: a function that consumes an ID only through a local variable is audited through the declaration it reads from (struct field, table, or public signature).

contract_note: Committed DEFAULT contract: the vanilla cap/count every checkout and the archival lane compile against. It is deliberately env-independent -- a build that opts into FE8_ITEM_ID_CAP>=0xCE reads the build-local ACTIVE contract (build/generated/data/id_space_active_audit.json and id_space_active.h) instead, and never rewrites this file.

chapter.record_count_note: no single record table: chapter data is authored per chapter in src/data/chapter_settings.h, so the cap -- not a record count -- is the contract

event.record_count_note: no record table: an event operand lane is a transport width, not a table of records

unit.record_count_note: no single record table: deployment slots are per-chapter event unit definitions; the 0x40 faction stride is the contract

domains.budget: 0 runtime bytes: already at the 8-bit storage ceiling.
domains.freeze_reason: Logical ID storage is a full 8-bit byte (GameSavePackedUnit.pid); 0x100+ needs a wider ID field across runtime and save, out of pilot scope.

domains.budget: 0 runtime bytes; capped at the 7-bit jid save field.
domains.freeze_reason: GameSavePackedUnit.jid is a 7-bit save bitfield; 0x80 silently truncates to 0x00 on save. Widening needs a save layout/epoch change, out of pilot scope.
domains.title: Class (job) ID

domains.budget: 0xCD->0xCE costs +1 struct ItemData record in ROM and 0 RAM/save-layout bytes: item save fields are already 14-bit (0x3FFF) and the runtime index is masked to 8 bits.
domains.default_behavior: Default cap 0xCD (206 vanilla records). Opt-in FE8_ITEM_ID_CAP raises the cap up to 0xFF.
